opportunities.title: Corrections Grade Tablets & Educational Software
opportunities.description: The County of San Mateo, Probation Department (the “County” and/or “Probation”) supports justice-involved youth by providing the mentorship and tools they need to succeed after detention. To enhance these efforts, we are seeking corrections-grade, tamper-resistant, rehabilitative tablets—secure mobile devices specifically designed to give detained youth access to vital educational and vocational resources. These tablets serve as a critical bridge for academic and vocational advancement, providing specialized preprogrammed software while maintaining essential family connectivity through strictly monitored, secure communication channels. Continuous oversight by Youth Services Center-Juvenile Hall (YSC-JH) staff ensures all interactions remain safe, appropriate and compliant with security protocols. In addition to supporting academic vocational and familial goals, the integration of vetted media – including movies and games - shall serve as key behavioral incentive to foster positive engagement and personal accountability. This comprehensive strategy reinforces vital support networks and cultivates the stability necessary for a successful reintegration into the community. The Probation Department is soliciting proposals from qualified vendors to deliver a comprehensive, secure and correction-grade tablet solution. The plan serves as a vital link between educational success, vocational growth and essential family support systems. The selected system must feature tamper-resistant hardware and pre-programmed, secure software for learning and monitored communication. By integrating strictly controlled family connectivity and vetted media (movies/games) as behavioral incentives, this initiative aims to maintain institutional security while providing youth with the digital tools and support networks essential for community reentry. This request seeks 50 units to achieve a 1-to-1 tablet-to-youth ratio allowing all youth to pursue a robust selection of courses like mathematics and resume writing, behavioral therapy and financial literacy modules. Additionally, the solution must facilitate the acquisition of trade-specific credentials and English as a Second Language (ESL) certifications to support career readiness and successful reentry. Furthermore, the selected vendor is required to provide initial on-site training and on-demand support for the duration of the contract. Additionally, a Dedicated Account Manager (DAM) shall be assigned to the Probation Department to facilitate regular progress meetings and ensure consistent ongoing assistance.

opportunities.title: Salesforce Test Automation
opportunities.description: San Mateo County is a dynamic and diverse county on the San Francisco Peninsula, spanning approximately 455 square miles between the Pacific Ocean and San Francisco Bay and serving nearly 800,000 residents across 20 incorporated cities and communities that range from dense urban centers to suburban neighborhoods and rural coastal areas. Established in April 1856, San Mateo County has grown into a nationally recognized hub of innovation and technology at the heart of Silicon Valley. The County boasts a thriving economy supported by industries such as bioscience, internet commerce, computer software, green technology, hospitality, financial management, health care, education, and transportation. What truly defines San Mateo County is its cultural, geographic, and economic diversity. The County is deeply committed to preserving its natural assets, nearly three-quarters of its land is open space, and agriculture continues to contribute to its economy and culture. San Mateo County provides essential services that protect and enhance the health, safety, welfare, and quality of life of all people, while embracing a tradition of public service, inclusion, and forward-thinking approaches to meeting community needs. The County has recently implemented a new Assessor Property Assessment System (APAS) to manage the assessment and valuation of properties with San Mateo County. As with any new system, changes and fixes are required as gaps and defects are identified through production usage. As these changes are deployed with new code, the staff within the Assessor Division of the Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder and Elections (ACRE) Department are currently performing highly complex UAT testing of highly detail multistep processes. Because the testing requires a high level of knowledge and expertise in the subject area, only a limited dedicated staff can perform such tests. And because the various modules are so intertwined with each other, a more thorough level of regression testing is also required. However, these staff also have other duties including operational support which limit available time to perform the testing. Thus, the Department is seeking an automated Salesforce testing solution which can increase their available bandwidth or possibly even offload the testing process to other less experienced staff.

opportunities.title: Liability Claims Adjusting Services RFP
opportunities.description: General work description: The Request for Proposal (RFP) seeks a qualified Third-Party Administrator (TPA) to provide comprehensive liability claims adjusting and administration services for the County of Sacramento's self-insured liability program. The selected contractor will work collaboratively with County Risk Management personnel to investigate, evaluate, negotiate, defend, settle, and resolve liability claims while ensuring timely reporting, cost-effective claim management, and compliance with County requirements, the Public Risk Innovation, Solutions, and Management (PRISM) Liability Claims Administration Standards, and applicable laws and regulations. The contractor will also provide strategic recommendations, maintain proactive communication, and support the County's objective of minimizing claim costs and liability exposure. The scope of work includes end-to-end administration of existing and new liability claims, including prompt investigations, reserve analysis, litigation management, settlement negotiations, payment processing, subrogation and recovery efforts, legal administration, claims reporting, records management, and financial oversight. The contractor will maintain a secure claims management information system, provide County staff with access to claims data, coordinate with defense counsel and subject matter experts, support regulatory and Medicare reporting requirements, prepare annual claims reports for the Board of Supervisors, and participate in regular meetings with County staff to review claim strategies, identify trends, and recommend loss prevention initiatives. The contractor must also provide rapid local response capabilities for significant incidents and ensure continuity throughout contract transitions. The successful proposer will demonstrate extensive experience administering liability claims for California public entities, particularly those involving public entity exposures such as law enforcement, employment practices, civil rights, and medical malpractice. Emphasis will be placed on the firm's technical qualifications, claims management processes, reporting capabilities, staffing, local support, financial controls, and overall methodology for delivering efficient, responsive, and high-quality claims administration services that protect the County's interests and ensure compliance with established standards and contractual requirements.

opportunities.title: Request for Proposals - Facilities Condition Assessment (FCA) and Asset Management Services for Sacramento County Department of Airports
opportunities.description: The County of Sacramento (County) owns and/or operates four airports in Sacramento County, including Sacramento International Airport (SMF or Airport), Mather Airport (MHR), Sacramento Executive Airport (SAC), and Franklin Field (F72) through the Department of Airports (SCDA or Department). The intent of this effort is to establish a reliable, decision-ready baseline of facility condition, asset lifecycle status, risk, and reinvestment needs across SMF, MHR, SAC, and F72. The services described in this RFP will support SCDA’s maintenance planning, Critical Equipment Replacement Program (CERP), and phased capital planning for short-term (0 to 5 years), mid-term (5 to 10 years), and long-term (10 to 20 years) priorities. A key outcome of this engagement is the delivery of accurate, structured asset and condition data that is fully compatible with SCDA’s enterprise platforms, including ProDIGIQ Asset Management System (AMS) and ProDIGIQ Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS). The data must support consistent asset hierarchies, condition scoring, and lifecycle modeling. The data must also align with SCDA’s existing ProDIGIQ AMS QR-code/barcode generation and asset identification standards, enabling scan-to-asset linkage for inspections, preventive maintenance, and work order history.

Annual training is mandated by regulatory bodies, including the Board of State and Community Corrections (BSCC), California Commission on Peace Officer Standards and Training (POST), and California Code of Regulations Title 15. opportunities.title: Establishment and Operation of Interim Housing for Families
opportunities.description: Through this Request for Information (RFI), the County of San Mateo (the County) Human Services Agency (HSA) Center on Homelessness (COH) seeks information from organizations that may be interested in establishing and/or operating an additional family interim housing program within San Mateo County Information gathered will assist the County in planning for expanded family interim housing capacity and a potential future solicitation for establishment and operation of one additional family interim housing program. This RFI is issued for information-gathering purposes only. No funds or contracts can or will be awarded through this RFI. This RFI is part of a market research effort to assess provider interest and capacity to add one family interim housing program in San Mateo County. The County is particularly interested in understanding: Whether qualified organizations are interested in operating a new family interim housing program; Whether qualified organizations are interested in procuring, leasing, acquiring, rehabilitating, developing, and/or constructing a facility for that purpose, including whether any already have a potential site in mind; Whether organizations would prefer to perform both the facility and operating roles, or perform one and partner with another organization; What supports, partnerships, or County involvement may be needed to make a project feasible. Information gathered through this process may inform program design, procurement strategy, service expectations, and a potential future Request for Proposals (RFP) or other solicitation. This RFI provides background on the County’s existing family shelter system, the need for additional family shelter capacity, and considerations for adding another family shelter program. Responses to this RFI are for informational and planning purposes only and do not obligate respondents to participate in any future procurement or take any other action. The County, through HSA’s COH, coordinates the homeless crisis response system. The system is designed to help individuals and families experiencing homelessness move toward stable housing. COH works countywide and collaborates with community-based organizations, public agencies, housing providers, and other stakeholders to strengthen the local homelessness response system. Family interim housing services are intended for households with children who are experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis and have no safe alternative housing options. In San Mateo County, these programs function as short-term, housing-focused interventions designed to provide a safe, decent, and family-appropriate place to stay while families stabilize, address immediate crises, and move as quickly as possible toward permanent housing. The County has not identified a specific region or facility for a new interim housing site. The County is seeking information from community-based organizations, shelter operators, housing and service providers, and other qualified entities with experience developing, establishing, and/or operating shelters or interim housing for families experiencing homelessness. The County is particularly interested in learning about provider capacity and considerations related to facility procurement and the provision of services relevant to adding another family shelter program to the County’s current system.

opportunities.description: Sacramento County Department of Health Services (DHS), Behavioral Health Services (BHS), is conducting an Open Enrollment to identify qualified individuals and organizations to provide psychiatric services for youth and young adults detained within Sacramento County’s Youth Detention Facility (YDF). The purpose of this Open Enrollment is to identify and contract with qualified psychiatrists to support County obligations under Title 15 of the California Code of Regulations, commencing with Article 8, Section 1400, Responsibility for Health Care Services (see Attachment A, Title 15 Minimum Standards for Juvenile Facilities). Psychiatry services under this Open Enrollment may include psychiatric assessment, diagnosis, and treatment; prescribing of psychotropic medications; medication evaluation, management, and monitoring; and consultation with YDF health and program staff. Services must be delivered safely, in a clinically appropriate manner, and in coordination with YDF multidisciplinary staff. Dispensing and administration of medications remains the responsibility of YDF health staff. Qualified providers are licensed physicians (M.D. or D.O.) who hold a current, active California medical license with board certification in psychiatry, and who are authorized to practice within the full scope of psychiatric medicine, including diagnosis and prescribing. Providers must be Board-Certified Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist, or board-eligible in child and adolescent psychiatry and actively pursuing board certification resulting in board-certification within 1 year of eligibility. Providers may contract individually or through a qualifying medical group or organization. All providers must adhere to applicable California laws, regulations, and professional standards of care. Contractors are required to comply with all regulatory requirements, facility policies and procedures, and expectations for coordination with YDF leadership and oversight entities.
